title: Author the Wave 1 acceptance tests as held-out red cases
description:
Objective: commit the epic's acceptance criteria as executable tests before any implementation task starts, so later tasks cannot quietly redefine what "delivered" means.

Deliverable: one new vitest file, packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts, holding one describe block per acceptance criterion from the epic description: fast QA cannot finish before candidate preparation; a failed required gate cannot release dependents; reviewing candidate A cannot approve B; restarting only the daemon during a long build preserves ownership; a delayed generation-N call cannot alter generation N+1; a crash between an external effect and its bookkeeping does not repeat the effect. Each case is written against the intended tool surface and marked it.skip with a comment naming the task that will unskip it. Assertions must be mutation-resistant: assert the exact rejected error code and the exact persisted record, never a truthy result.

Not in scope: any production code, any tool registration, any schema change. This task adds exactly one file.

These tests are held out. Implementation tasks unskip their own case and must make it pass unchanged; a diff that edits the assertion instead of the code is a QA reject.

Verification: npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon, showing the expected skipped count and zero failures.
definitionOfDone: packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts exists with one skipped case per acceptance criterion in the epic description, six in total
Each case names, in a comment, the sibling task expected to unskip it
Every assertion checks an exact error code or an exact persisted field, with no truthiness-only assertions
npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts reports six skipped and zero failed
The daemon suite stays green: npm test in packages/moe-daemon
taskRails: Tests only. This task must not touch production code, tools/index.ts, or schema.ts.
Later tasks unskip these cases; they must never edit the assertions to pass.

implementationPlan.description: AUTHOR THE SHARED FIXTURE AND THE ARTIFACT-BOUNDARY CASE. Load test-driven-development and re-read the delivered tool contracts, retaining foreign WIP. Create ONLY packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts: six describes named for the epic criteria, one it.skip callback each, no extra tests. All fixture creation, processes and future-tool lookup happen inside callbacks, never on collection. Reuse existing ToolTestHarness, StateManager, getTools and MoeError; invoke registered handlers through state.runExclusive rather than fake business handlers. Missing future registration must throw a diagnostic when unskipped, never return a passing fallback; no static import of an absent module. Define small file-local JSON fixture/read/projection and cleanup helpers, not a production adapter or copied delivery algorithm. The file header records the human-confirmed pilot (Codex exec; local branch refs/heads/wave1-pilot), the exact contracts in this plan, and the six unskip owners. First case owner: task-d72d8cc6a29a4181a3767f493007320e. Using legacy/default delivery policy, create worker W, coding task A with a completed step and task B pending; claim A, fetch context, and call real complete_task with valid verification/summary. Capture the returned attemptId/generation from claim and assert disk A.status=REVIEW and the sole attempts record {taskId:A,workerId:W,generation:1,phase:'finalizing'}. Fast human-path qa_approve(A,summary) and W's claim of B must each reject with MoeError code -32002, codeName ATTEMPT_FINALIZING, context.attemptId=<A attempt>, context.retryable=true; task/attempt persisted bytes must remain unchanged. New normative finalize_attempt payload is {taskId,workerId,runnerId,attemptId,generation,outcome:'landed',landedRevision:<40-hex SHA>}. Call it twice, asserting one attempt remains, phase closed, generation 1 and second-call disk bytes unchanged; W can then claim B, whose assignedWorkerId is W. Do not require Candidate/Receipt APIs in this early case. The header must document the governor-confirmed split: prerequisite task-5dd49fe2f31b477bbbad581dd22dd9af provides the minimal qa_approve finalizing hold; task-d72d8cc6a29a4181a3767f493007320e supplies finalization and unskips this combined case. No Candidate/Receipt dependency, delivery-policy broadening or mock approval.
implementationPlan.note: Created the single deliverable file with the frozen header (pilot = Codex exec + local branch refs/heads/wave1-pilot, normative payload/codeName contracts, six unskip owners, six old-behaviour counterexamples) plus file-local helpers: requireTool (exactly-one registered production tool by exact MCP name, loud [WAVE1-CONTRACT-MISSING] diagnostic otherwise, no static import of an absent module), callTool (state.runExclusive, real handlers), captureRefusal (exact code/codeName/context, fails on a resolved promise or a non-MoeError), readBytes/readJson/listRecords/project, deterministic 40-hex SHA literals. Verified live before writing: getTools/ToolDefinition/ToolHandler in tools/index.ts, MoeError+codeName in util/errors.ts (NOT types/errors.ts), StateManager.runExclusive/clearEmitter, ToolTestHarness init/setupMoeFolder/createEpic/createTask/createWorker/cleanup, completeTask's assertAllStepsCompleted+assertVerificationEvidence, claim_next_task explicit-taskId path. Confirmed absent today: src/delivery/, moe.finalize_attempt, moe.reattach_attempt, moe.record_candidate, moe.record_check_run, moe.record_delivery_receipt, settings.deliveryPolicy. Case 1 (owner task-d72d8cc6a29a4181a3767f493007320e, prereq task-5dd49fe2f31b477bbbad581dd22dd9af) authored under legacy/default policy, no Candidate/Receipt dependency: claim A -> generation 1, complete_task -> disk REVIEW + sole attempt {taskId,workerId,generation:1,phase:'finalizing'}, fast qa_approve AND the worker's claim of B both refused -32002/ATTEMPT_FINALIZING with context.attemptId + context.retryable=true and byte-identical task/attempt files, then finalize_attempt {taskId,workerId,runnerId,attemptId,generation,outcome:'landed',landedRevision} twice -> one attempt, phase closed, generation 1, second call byte-identical, then B claimable with assignedWorkerId=W. All fixtures/tool lookups inside the callback; cleanup clears the emitter in finally. npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts -> 1 skipped, 0 failed. Shared checkout: pre-existing foreign dirty paths (.moe/tasks peers, .moe/epics, .moe/resources, packages/moe-daemon/src/providers) left untouched.

implementationPlan.description: AUTHOR THE FAILED-GATE DEPENDENCY CASE. Owner comment: task-94f534924ea841af8c164191060ee4d3. Freeze the strict pilot configuration as settings.deliveryPolicy='local-branch' with existing autoCommit=true, consolidationBranch='wave1-pilot', qualityGate='node gate.cjs', qualityGateScope='everyTask', autoCreateBranch=false and checkpointPush=false. Use exact persisted fixture records loaded through StateManager: DONE prerequisite P, current Candidate C (fields id,attemptId,taskId,baseRevision,treeSha,deliveryTarget,createdAt), matching successful Review and local receipt, and its required CheckRun {id,candidateId:C,treeSha:C.treeSha,command:'node gate.cjs',exitCode:1,outputTail:'gate failed',runnerId,source:'runner-observed'}. Also include a passing check for an older/different candidate so a task-wide any-pass lookup cannot satisfy the oracle. Create D WORKING/unassigned with dependsOn:[P] and E BLOCKED/unassigned with blockedOnTaskIds:[P], blockedFromStatus:'WORKING'. Calling real explicit claim_next_task(D) must reject -32003/DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING with context.prerequisiteTaskId=P and context.missingEvidence=['required-check:node gate.cjs']; D and E persisted state must be unchanged. Invoke existing runDependencyUnblock under state.runExclusive and prove E remains BLOCKED with its hold fields intact. Record an agent-reported pass for C through real record_check_run and repeat the refusal/hold assertions; then record a runner-observed pass for the same C/tree/command and prove real claim assigns D and the same unblock path restores E to WORKING. Set all other evidence valid initially so these tests isolate failed/missing authoritative gate evidence, not an unrelated absent receipt or review. All failed paths compare exact task/check bytes or exact projected fields, including source and exitCode; never substitute agent verification.exitCode for CheckRun evidence.
implementationPlan.note: Case 2 authored (owner task-94f534924ea841af8c164191060ee4d3). Frozen STRICT_SETTINGS = deliveryPolicy 'local-branch' + existing autoCommit=true, consolidationBranch 'wave1-pilot', qualityGate 'node gate.cjs', qualityGateScope 'everyTask', autoCreateBranch=false, checkpointPush=false (spelled out in full because setupMoeFolder replaces the whole settings object). Fixture writes exact persisted records into the temp .moe/ before state.load(): DONE P; current Candidate cand-P-current {id,attemptId,taskId,baseRevision,treeSha,deliveryTarget,createdAt}; valid Review + local receipt for it; its runner-observed CheckRun exitCode 1 'gate failed'; plus an OLDER candidate cand-P-old on a different tree with a passing runner-observed check so a task-wide any-pass lookup cannot satisfy the oracle. D WORKING/unassigned dependsOn [P]; E BLOCKED/unassigned blockedOnTaskIds [P], blockedFromStatus WORKING. assertStillHeld: explicit claim_next_task(D) -> -32003/DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING, context.prerequisiteTaskId='task-P', context.missingEvidence=['required-check:node gate.cjs']; runDependencyUnblock under state.runExclusive returns [] and E keeps exact {status BLOCKED, assignedWorkerId null, blockedOnTaskIds [P], blockedFromStatus WORKING}; D, E and the failed check byte-identical. Run after the failed gate, and again after a real record_check_run agent-reported pass (whose persisted projection incl. source+exitCode is asserted). Positive control: a runner-observed pass for the same candidate/tree/command lets the real claim assign D to worker-N and the same unblock path returns ['task-E'] with E WORKING and hold fields null. Imported existing runDependencyUnblock (exported, verified); typed the step fixture as ImplementationStep and dropped needless casts. Focused run: 2 skipped, 0 failed.

implementationPlan.description: AUTHOR THE CANDIDATE-SWAP REVIEW CASE. Owner comment: task-5b85773867594a8eb0cea350f2c6008f. Use default/legacy policy to isolate candidate binding from strict delivery gates. Fixture begins after complete_task with task A REVIEW/unassigned and its generation-1 attempt finalizing. Real record_candidate accepts {id,taskId,attemptId,generation,workerId,baseRevision,treeSha,deliveryTarget}; use 40-hex distinct trees, fixed IDs and deterministically ordered creation times. Record candidate A; get_context must project the exact stored record at result.currentCandidate, and retain its id as the reviewed token. Record different candidate B with a later creation time for the same task/attempt; finalize the matching attempt with B's landing outcome so the fast-QA hold is no longer the refusing layer. Call real qa_approve with candidateId=A, summary and a registered QA workerId on the unassigned review task. Require -32002/CANDIDATE_MISMATCH with context.expectedCandidateId=A and context.currentCandidateId=B, byte-identical task and both candidate records, and no persisted approval Review. Then approve with candidateId=B and require disk task.status=DONE plus exactly one Review under reviews/, with exact {taskId, candidateId:B, reviewerId:<QA id>, decision:'approve', summary:<submitted summary>}; A's immutable bytes remain unchanged. The new currentCandidate projection selects the latest recorded candidate deterministically by createdAt then id; no task-wide cached approval or caller token replacement. Isolate any Date-only fake clock to this callback and restore it. The assertion constants remain independent of the production selector.
implementationPlan.note: Case 3 authored (owner task-5b85773867594a8eb0cea350f2c6008f), legacy/default policy. Fixture starts where complete_task leaves A: REVIEW/unassigned plus a persisted generation-1 attempt in phase finalizing (new typed attemptRecord helper builds the exact ExecutionAttempt shape attemptStore writes; loaded by StateManager.load from .moe/attempts). Registered coder worker-W and QA qa-Q. Date-only fake clock (timers stay real per the attemptStore rename-backoff gotcha), restored in finally. Real record_candidate for cand-A {id,taskId,attemptId,generation,workerId,baseRevision,treeSha,deliveryTarget} -> disk record equals payload + createdAt 03:00:00Z; get_context result.currentCandidate equals the exact stored record. cand-B (distinct tree, createdAt 03:05:00Z) -> currentCandidate now equals B's stored record. finalize_attempt with B's landing removes the criterion-1 hold as the refusing layer. qa_approve {candidateId:'cand-A'} -> -32002/CANDIDATE_MISMATCH, context.expectedCandidateId 'cand-A', context.currentCandidateId 'cand-B', task + both candidates byte-identical, reviews/ empty. Positive control: qa_approve {candidateId:'cand-B'} -> disk DONE and exactly one Review projecting {taskId, candidateId:'cand-B', reviewerId:'qa-Q', decision:'approve', summary}; cand-A bytes unchanged. Assertion constants are literals, independent of any production selector. Also in this step: made writeRecord generic over {id:string}; case 1's fast QA call now omits workerId to match the plan's human-path qa_approve(A, summary). Focused run: 3 skipped, 0 failed.

implementationPlan.description: AUTHOR THE DAEMON-RESTART OWNERSHIP CASE. Owner comment: task-58f7db9a9e44469e9351b2cdea73b47d. Test actual daemon startup, not merely StateManager.load: launch a fixture-only child using the installed tsx CLI with absolute src/index.ts, '_run', '--project', isolated project, '--port', a dynamically selected free port and '--host','127.0.0.1'; use daemon.json plus /health readiness and JSON-RPC over /mcp. Do not run the production repo daemon, supervisor, build/prebuild or default fleet port. Keep a separate silent long-build Node child alive with an explicit ready handshake; its start timestamp and host match the persisted attempt. Seed worker W and a running generation-1 attempt under workers/ and attempts/ in the temporary fixture, start daemon and attach, then abruptly kill ONLY the daemon child and await exit before starting a second daemon over the same fixture. During restart hold require persisted task.assignedWorkerId=W and status WORKING, worker.currentTaskId unchanged, exactly one attempt with same id/generation and phase reconciling. A competing explicit coding claim must reject -32002/ATTEMPT_RECONCILING with context.attemptId equal to the held attempt, leaving these records unchanged. Define the new runner surface moe.reattach_attempt({taskId,workerId,runnerId,attemptId,generation,processStartedAt,host}); a mismatched processStartedAt rejects -32002/ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH without writes, the matching identity restores phase running while retaining worker/task ownership and generation 1. Confirm the build child never exited, then stop it only in finally. Do not infer death from old lastActivityAt or wait for a reconcile timeout. Use bounded condition polling/child exit promises, not fixed sleeps; propagate child startup/health/transport failures with captured bounded output, never turn them into skipped/passing assertions.
implementationPlan.note: Case 4 authored (owner task-58f7db9a9e44469e9351b2cdea73b47d). Real startup, not a StateManager reload: process.execPath + installed tsx CLI (node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs) + absolute src/index.ts '_run' --project <temp> --port <dynamic free port> --host 127.0.0.1, HOME/USERPROFILE/TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR redirected into an owned temp root, MOE_*/GIT_* fleet vars stripped, Git config isolated. Readiness = daemon.json naming a NEW pid whose /health answers 200 with the same pid; JSON-RPC over a fresh ws /mcp per call. Seeds task L WORKING/W with an IN_PROGRESS step, worker W CODING currentTaskId L with lastActivityAt 3h old (quiet != dead), attempt-L-1 running gen 1 whose processStartedAt/host come from a separate silent long-build Node child's ready handshake. Daemon #1 boots, runner attaches via moe.reattach_attempt -> phase running; daemon killed abruptly by its daemon.json pid (tsx launcher awaited), build child asserted alive; daemon #2 boots over the same fixture. Hold: task WORKING/W, worker.currentTaskId L, exactly one attempt same id/gen 1 phase reconciling. Competing claim by worker-X -> wire code -32002, data.codeName ATTEMPT_RECONCILING, data.tool, message names attempt-L-1; task/worker/attempt bytes unchanged. Mismatched processStartedAt -> -32002/ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, bytes unchanged. Matching identity -> phase running, generation 1, ownership retained; build child exitCode/signalCode null and pid alive. DEVIATION to flag: McpAdapter forwards only data {tool, codeName}, never MoeError.context (McpAdapter.test.ts:220 pins exactly those keys), so over the wire the held attempt id is asserted via the refusal message instead of context.attemptId; no transport change is demanded of the owner. Helpers added (file-local, no delivery decisions): spawnOwned/awaitExit/stopOwned/waitFor (bounded polling, throws abort), isPidAlive, freePort, makeOwnedRoot/removeOwnedRoot (refuses anything not a prefixed direct child of os.tmpdir()), isolatedEnv, startDaemonChild, killDaemonAbruptly, stopFixtureDaemons, mcpRequest/daemonTool/toolResult/toolRefusal, withTeardown (teardown never masks the body's failure). Helper smoke: a throwaway unskipped copy (deleted, never committed) booted a real fixture daemon in 1.3s, got 'Tool not found: moe.reattach_attempt' (-32601, a hard failure in toolResult, not a pass), parsed a wire refusal, killed daemon pid 71548 (launcher 51904 relayed exit 1), restarted, listed workers, removed both roots; tasklist confirms both daemon pids gone. That run also showed today's counterexample: after boot task L was unassigned and workers/ empty. Focused run: 4 skipped, 0 failed.

implementationPlan.description: AUTHOR THE DELAYED-GENERATION MUTATION CASE. Owner comment: task-b6c48bf029bf4170a603a91c12451df7 (lifecycle wiring, not guard-only task-a135d4d6). Real claim_next_task accepts optional runnerId/workspace/processStartedAt/host and returns top-level attemptId and generation; retain those exact tokens. Start a WORKING task with a pending step and no step lease. Worker W claims generation 1, deliberately releases through release_task with {taskId,workerId:W,attemptId:<N id>,generation:1,reason:<explicit handoff>}, and claims the SAME task again as W, yielding generation 2 and a new attempt id. Snapshot task, worker and both attempt files AFTER the second claim. Deliver the delayed identical generation-1 release request: it must throw -32002/ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED (the sibling guard's approved stable code), not an ownership error, since W still owns the task. Require every captured file byte-identical, task still WORKING/assigned W, N phase closed, N+1 phase running/generation 2, exactly two attempts and no added handoff. Finally release using N+1 identity and prove its persisted phase closes normally. This positive control prevents a blanket release refusal from satisfying the test. No force takeover, no mutated in-memory fixture after capture, and no assertion that generation fencing stops an external process writing shared files.
implementationPlan.note: Case 5 authored (owner task-b6c48bf029bf4170a603a91c12451df7, explicitly not guard-only task-a135d4d6). WORKING task G with one PENDING step and no lease; W claims via real claim_next_task with runnerId/workspace -> top-level attemptId N, generation 1; deliberate release_task {taskId, workerId W, attemptId N, generation 1, reason 'Explicit handoff…', handoffNote} (handoffNote added so 'no added handoff' is a live check: priorHandoffs goes to exactly 1); W re-claims the SAME task -> generation 2, new attempt id (asserted != N). Snapshot task, worker, attempt N and attempt N+1 bytes after the second claim. Replaying the identical generation-1 release -> -32002/ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED (not an ownership error: W still owns the task); all four files byte-identical, task WORKING/assigned W, priorHandoffs still 1, exactly two attempts, N {generation 1, phase closed}, N+1 {generation 2, phase running}. Positive control: release with the N+1 identity closes N+1 (phase closed, generation 2), task WORKING/unassigned, still two attempts — a blanket release refusal cannot satisfy the case. No force flag, no in-memory mutation after capture, and the describe comment states fencing guards daemon state only. Focused run: 5 skipped, 0 failed.

implementationPlan.description: AUTHOR THE CRASH-AFTER-REF-MOVE REPLAY CASE. Owner comment: task-b1c9850824fe4437a8c70b4ee083602b. Execute the actual platform wrapper, not a copied recovery algorithm: PowerShell scripts/moe-agent.ps1 with -Project <temp> -WorkerId <stable W> -Role worker -Command <temp codex.cmd> -CodexExec -NoStartDaemon -NoLoop -PollInterval 0; macOS/Linux scripts/moe-agent.sh with equivalent --project/--worker-id/--role/--command/--codex-exec/--no-start-daemon/--no-loop/--poll-interval 0. Generate the provider shim and transport shim only at test runtime in the fixture: the Codex shim answers version/help probes and, on its real exec invocation, edits only declared owned.txt and calls actual get_context/start_step/complete_step/complete_task via the fixture endpoint. Transport uses MOE_PROXY_PATH and forwards JSON-RPC to the existing production McpAdapter.handle over a loopback HTTP fixture server; never fake claim/complete/candidate/check/receipt business responses. Use one isolated Git repository with fixed identity, initial base commit on wave1-pilot, the strict policy from case 2 and an owned tracked gate.cjs. The real wrapper freezes/records/checks/lands. Intercept ONLY the first record_delivery_receipt request: before forwarding it, verify the actual target ref has moved from base to the request's landed revision and its tree equals the recorded candidate tree, signal the barrier, and keep the request pending. Abruptly terminate the wrapper's own child tree (no graceful deregistration trap), proving receipts/ has zero records. Restart fixture StateManager/McpAdapter from disk and rerun the SAME production wrapper, worker and repository with interception disabled and the retained production recovery state; do not manufacture a receipt or rerun the landing in the fixture. Assert exactly one post-base target ref movement/commit in Git's persisted history, final target unchanged from the first movement, candidate/required successful CheckRun still bind the same tree/base, exactly one receipt with {candidateId,target:'refs/heads/wave1-pilot',targetBefore:<base>,targetAfter:<first landed SHA>,landedRevision:<first landed SHA>,pushResult:null}, and owning attempt closed without a successor generation. Replaying record_delivery_receipt with the same captured payload must leave its bytes/count unchanged. Fail with bounded logs if the receipt barrier is never reached; missing future implementation is not a test success. No new production hook or wrapper test mode is needed.
implementationPlan.note: Case 6 authored (owner task-b1c9850824fe4437a8c70b4ee083602b). Executes the ACTUAL platform wrapper: pwsh (fallback powershell.exe) -File scripts/moe-agent.ps1 -Project <temp> -WorkerId worker-pilot -Role worker -Command <temp codex.cmd> -CodexExec -NoStartDaemon -NoLoop -PollInterval 0 on Windows; bash scripts/moe-agent.sh with the equivalent long flags (own process group) elsewhere. Runtime-generated shims only: MOE_PROXY_PATH transport shim (stdin JSON-RPC -> POST -> stdout line) and a Codex shim (codex.cmd -> node codex-shim.cjs; shebang file on POSIX) that answers --version/--help probes and on exec edits only declared owned.txt and drives real get_context/start_step/complete_step/complete_task, inert when the task is no longer WORKING for it. The loopback fixture transport forwards every request to the production McpAdapter.handle; its only other behaviour is holding the FIRST moe.record_delivery_receipt pending, capturing git rev-parse of the target and of the request's landedRevision tree. Isolated repo with fixed identity, base commit on refs/heads/wave1-pilot (gate.cjs passes only when owned.txt carries the delivery marker; .moe/ and .codex/ ignored), STRICT_SETTINGS. At the barrier: target == request landedRevision, its parent == base, the recorded candidate {id, taskId, baseRevision base, treeSha == landed tree, deliveryTarget} and exactly one runner-observed exit-0 CheckRun for that candidate/tree. Whole-tree kill (taskkill /T /F or group SIGKILL), receipts/ == []. Fixture StateManager/McpAdapter restarted from disk, interception off, SAME wrapper rerun. Then: target still the first landing, rev-list base..target == [landed], reflog == [landed, base], exactly one receipt {candidateId, target refs/heads/wave1-pilot, targetBefore base, targetAfter/landedRevision landed, pushResult null}, candidate + check bytes unchanged, attempts == [{taskId, workerId, generation 1, phase closed}], and replaying the captured receipt payload through McpAdapter.handle leaves the single receipt byte-identical. Barrier never reached => named failure with wrapper output tail, fixture RPC log and shim argv log. Smoke (throwaway unskipped copy, deleted): today's wrapper ran the full pre-flight through the transport, the argv probe hit the shim, the shim completed task-R, the real wrapper passed the gate and committed fb775dea on wave1-pilot, push failed (no origin, WARN only), then the case failed exactly as designed: 'wrapper run 1 exited ({code:0}) without calling moe.record_delivery_receipt: the receipt barrier was never reached'. Teardown removed both temp roots; no pwsh left running. Also added withDeadline (awaitExit now uses it). Focused run: 6 skipped, 0 failed.

implementationPlan.description: FINAL ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW AND QA HANDOFF. Load adversarial-self-review; review only acceptance.test.ts as a hostile implementation author. Can any case pass if the handler is unregistered, permanently refuses, mutates before throwing, approves a different candidate, reuses an agent-reported/other-tree gate, merely reloads state while skipping real startup, replaces the wrapper with a counter, or retries a Git effect then hides the duplicate? Positive controls and exact disk/ref assertions must kill each. Preserve the six independent owners and the assertion contract; no placeholders, swallowed exceptions, broad truthiness/snapshot or expect.any assertions, hidden test.skip-on-error, live-repo state fixtures, production/schema/registry/harness edits or new dependencies. Task-local transport/process helpers belong in this one file and may not implement delivery decisions.
